items: T5 Judgment — Confirm prior-art coverage for every affected path, including merged and closed/rejected work — the brief reports a CLI history query and broad src/targets search, but this single-commit target has no remotes or review history to independently establish complete coverage; brief.md:26 and patch.diff:111.

`gate-logs/T2-threat-model.log` and `check-gates.json` T2 row: the gate reports "no security-relevant path touched". This patch adds `targets/ubuntu-26.04/allowlist.toml`, which the brief itself calls the file that decides what runs without a confirm (human-only review). It also adds nothing to the threat model. T2's path classifier doesn't know about `targets/*/allowlist.toml`, so its green result is not real evidence. Treat the allowlist entries as unreviewed by any gate. The human should decide whether to widen T2's path list and whether the threat model needs a §Trusted entry for `targets/`.

**Critical (conditional on how #12 parses `+` words)**, `targets/ubuntu-26.04/allowlist.toml:338-340` (`[commands.less]`). **Input:** a model proposal (untrusted, item 5). **What goes wrong:** `less` treats any argument that starts with `+` as an initial command, and that command can be `!cmd` (run a shell command), `|` (pipe to a command) or `v` (open an editor). Spec §1.1 allows a LF inside quotes in a proposal. So a proposal like `less '+!touch /tmp/pwned<LF>q' README.md` is just `less` plus one operand under §6.2, with no `-` option. The entry has no `max_operands` and no field that can forbid `+` words, so unless the #12 gate treats `+…` as an unlisted option, this runs a program with no confirm. **Reproduced here:** `script -qc "less '+!touch ./pwned-by-less<LF>q' in.txt"` created `./pwned-by-less` (less 668). The brief's rule (Scope (2)) is "if no §6.2 shape is safe, leave the word off — decided here, not by Do". That makes this a brief/spec decision, not a builder fix. Options: (a) leave `less` off v1, as was done for `command` and `ip`; (b) state in spec §6.2 that a word starting with `+` counts as an option (so it is unlisted, so `mutating`) for `less`/`more`, and pin that for #12; (c) have #12 always run `less` with `LESSSECURE=1`. `more` (`:342-344`) only takes `+NUM`/`+/pattern` and is not affected the same way.

**High**, `targets/ubuntu-26.04/allowlist.toml:335-344, 379-383, 392-393` (`man`, `less`, `dpkg`/`dpkg-query`, `vulkaninfo`), against spec `policy-gate/v1` §3 and §7.5. **Input:** session environment (items 3 and 4). For example, a repo script the user confirmed as `source scripts/env.sh`, or a direnv `.envrc`, sets a variable that these entries read but that the §7.5 baseline check (`PAGER`, `MANPAGER`, `SYSTEMD_PAGER`, `GIT_PAGER`, `LESSOPEN`, `LESSCLOSE`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`) does not cover. A later "read-only" proposal then runs code with no confirm, and the gate never sees the session change. **Reproduced here:** `LESS='+!touch ./pwned-by-LESS-env<LF>q' less in.txt` created the file. The same class covers `MANOPT` (man-db reads options from it, including `-P`/`-H`, the very options this entry excludes), `DPKG_PAGER` (used by `dpkg -l`/`dpkg-query -l` on a terminal), `VK_LAYER_PATH`/`VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` (make `vulkaninfo` load an arbitrary shared library), and `LD_AUDIT` (only `LD_PRELOAD`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are snapshotted). This is a spec gap, not a builder bug. This diff is the first allowlist to depend on it, and the allowlist header (`:333-334`) claims the pager variables are covered by §7.5. A human should decide whether to extend the §3/§7.5 variable lists (in #12 or a spec amendment) or to hold back these words until they are extended.

**The Scope asks for restrictions that the format test (g) forbids.** Scope (2) says "Encode every restriction the table states (`date` only `+FORMAT`, … `command` only with `-v`)". Test (g) says the allowlist "uses only the spec §6.2 entry fields". Spec §6.2 (`v1.md:137-142`) allows only `flags`, `options`, `subcommands`, `max_operands` and `stdin`. Several required restrictions cannot be written with those fields:

**The security-relevant part of the allowlist has no test.** Criterion (g) checks the command-word set and the field names only. None of the restrictions the brief lists is checked by a test: `xxd` has no `-r`, `sort` has no `-o`/`--output`/`--compress-program`, `env`/`printenv` have `max_operands = 0`, the `systemctl`/`apt`/`apt-cache`/`dpkg` subcommand lists match §6.4 exactly, and `journalctl` has no `--vacuum-*`/`--rotate`/`--flush`. An allowlist with `xxd` `flags = ["-r"]` or `sort` `options = ["-o"]` passes the gate. Given "an extra one can run code unconfirmed" (brief Scope (2)), a few negative assertions should go into (g) for the restrictions the table states. Otherwise the only check on this is human review at sign-off.

**The brief bases the work on `main`, but criterion (c) needs #14, which isn't merged.** The brief says "Repo + branch target: eduralph/nl-shell @ main" and "Depends on: 14". `dependency-state.json` lists #14 as `PLANNED`, not merged. `src/nl_shell/repl.py:33-62` on `main` has no `:status`, so (c) "`:status` shows both the target id and the mismatch" and Scope (5) can't be done or tested on `main`. Citations expected also says to cite the `:status` block "on the wave base". The brief should say whether this is "Stacks on: 14", with #14's branch as the base, or whether Do waits for #14 to merge. As written, Do could start from `main` with no `:status` to extend. The C4 red leg would then revert a `repl.py` that has no `:status`, and that only works if the base includes #14.

**The brief overrides the issue's "code outside `targets/` must not name an OS", and it misses one place.** The issue body says "Code outside `targets/` must not name an OS." ADR-0023 uses MUST (`0023-os-targets.md:51`). The brief puts the tagline in `src/nl_shell/__init__.py:1` and `src/nl_shell/cli.py:14` (`description="Natural-language shell for Ubuntu 26.04."`) out of scope, and leaves it as an Open question it answers "no" to. It doesn't list `pyproject.toml:8`, which has the same tagline. Scope (6) only stops OS-specific *values* in code, and no test checks that. Either a maintainer approves this exception before Do starts, or the brief adds a check, for example "no `ubuntu`/`26.04` literal in `src/` except the named tagline lines". Without that, criterion (6) can't be checked.

**The `config.toml` unit is extra scope that belongs to #77.** The issue only asks that `target =` in `config.toml` names a target. Scope (4) and criterion (d) add more: a separate config-reading unit, XDG path handling, "a malformed `config.toml` is refused with a message", and a rule that unknown keys are ignored. That is a new refusal path and a module boundary chosen for #77/#62/#16 folds. Combined with the ~70-entry allowlist translation, which the brief's own Open question says may need to be its own slice, this is three reviewable changes in one bundle: loader and selection, config unit, and allowlist content. Consider moving the allowlist content into its own slice now rather than "if review looks too large". It is the human-only-review surface (INTEGRATION §4, `v1.md:204-206`), and the loader code shouldn't wait on it.

**(Minor) The criterion says "degraded", but nothing can observe it yet.** The issue's Done-when asks for "a mismatched `--target` (degraded)". Spec §7.7 (`v1.md:197-198`) defines degraded as a gate behaviour, and the gate is #12 and out of scope. Test (c) can only check a recorded flag, a reason string, a warning and a `:status` line. That is fine if a human agrees it meets the issue's "degraded" wording. Say it explicitly at sign-off so the issue isn't closed on a claim the code can't show yet.

C1 Spec — Approve the tagline exception to the no-OS-in-code rule and accepting recorded mismatch before #12 implements degraded execution — these qualify the advertised completion scope; target/docs/design/adr/0023-os-targets.md:51, target/docs/design/adr/0023-os-targets.md:72, target/src/nl_shell/cli.py:14, brief.md:61.

C5 Causal adequacy — Decide whether retaining pagers pending #12 is acceptable — rejecting executable `+` words is an undischarged dependency; evidence currently pins a comment and absent flags, not actual rejection by a gate; target/targets/ubuntu-26.04/allowlist.toml:341, target/tests/test_targets.py:554.

T5 Judgment — Confirm affected-path prior art across merged history and closed/rejected work — the brief records a partial path-based search, but this one-commit copy has no remote or PR history to independently establish coverage of all affected files; brief.md:26, patch.diff:1, patch.diff:51, patch.diff:226.

`src/nl_shell/cli.py:28-38` with `src/nl_shell/os_release.py:82-91`: `--target` can't get past an os-release file that exists but can't be read, though it does get past a missing one. Reproduced with fakes. If `/etc/os-release` is a directory (or unreadable) and the user passes `--target ubuntu-26.04`, nl-shell exits 1 with "can't be read". If neither os-release file exists, the same command starts the REPL in the mismatch state ("detected: unknown unknown"). Either way the session would be in mismatch (degraded) mode, where every command needs a confirm. So starting would be safe, and refusing takes away the user's only way out. Brief case (c) only says "on a non-matching OS → starts" and doesn't cover this. Low severity. The human should decide whether a named target should also start, in mismatch mode, when os-release can't be read.

**High (a session change the gate misses, which then leads to "a non-read-only command runs with no confirm"),** `targets/ubuntu-26.04/allowlist.toml:907-925` (`man`, `less`, `more`), `:929-940` (`systemctl`, `journalctl`, which open a pager) and `:960-964` (`dpkg`, `dpkg-query`). The file bans `-P`/`--pager`/`-H` on `man` and lists no `+` words for `less`. Its comment says the rest is covered because "pager variables must match the baseline (§7.5)". But §7.5 (`docs/design/specs/policy-gate/v1.md:193-194`) only checks `PAGER`, `MANPAGER`, `SYSTEMD_PAGER`, `GIT_PAGER`, `LESSOPEN`, `LESSCLOSE` and the loader variables. Three other variables put back exactly what the entries ban, and §3 (`v1.md:98-101`) doesn't list them as session-altering either:
